per_claim.claim: R1: Residue-thread / class-pair criterion. Unimodality of A(q)[b]_{q^r} is decided by alternating partial sums of (1-q)A(q) sampled along arithmetic progressions of step r ('class pairs').
per_claim.evidence:
The criterion as stated was not found. Closest ingredients, each opened and quoted:
(1) ProveIt report.tex, Lemma 4.1 ('The periodic tail') (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex): 'If $n\ge\max\{1,S-r+2\}$, then $u_n-u_{n-1}=\delta_{n\bmod r}$. If also $n<rb$, the same difference occurs in $P=F\qir b r$', where 'R_s=\sum_{0\le j\le S, j\equiv s (r)} f_j' and '\delta_s=R_s-R_{s-1}'. So ProveIt computes first differences of P as sums of differences of F along the residue class of n, i.e. (1-q)F sampled on a progression of step r. It does this only in the tail range n>=S-r+2 and uses it only as a necessary condition (Thm 4.2). It has no alternating partial sums, no class pairs and no iff criterion.
(2) AI-Has-Taste main.tex (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArtificialZeng/AI-Has-Taste/main/reproducible_source_code/BigWIN2/BW2-PR20260914-q_product_unimodality/source/manuscript/main.tex), k=2 only: '\Delta_n=N(n-a+1,n)-N(n-a-c+1,n-c)' with N counting j in [0,b-1] with rj in a window. This is an exact difference formula for two ordinary factors, in counting form, not a general class-pair criterion.
(3) Xin-Zhong, arXiv:1912.01829 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01829), abstract: 'We conjecture that they are unimodal with respect to parity, or equivalently, $(1+q)C_{m+n}(q)$ is unimodal.' This is an adjacent idea: coefficients sampled along residue classes mod 2 are tied to unimodality after multiplying by a q-integer. It concerns [2]_q and q-Catalan polynomials, not [b]_{q^r}.
(4) Abdallah-McDaniel, ALCO 8(2) (2025) 295-317 (https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.414): 'complex Hodge-Riemann relations (complex HRR) to mean that the maps in Equation (3) have signature equal to the alternating sum of even first differences of the Hilbert function.' This is an alternating sum of first differences along one parity class, for the Hilbert function prod_i [m]_{t^i}. It is a representation and Lefschetz invariant, not a unimodality criterion for f(q)[b]_{q^r}.
Differences from R1: no source states an iff criterion for general A and r via alternating class sums.

per_claim.claim: R2: Parity/closure structure. U = [1,N*] ∪ {N*+2, N*+4, ..., beta}, max U ≡ 1+F (mod 2), and b in U implies b-2 in U.
per_claim.evidence:
The general structure was not found. Every complete classification in the literature gives an interval U=[1,B*], which is the gap-free case of R2. In each, B*-1-F is even, matching max U ≡ 1+F (mod 2):
(a) CIMSY arXiv:2605.12822 Prop 5.3 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12822): 'Let $a,b,r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. Then $[a]_{q}[b]_{q^{r}}$ is unimodal if and only if $a\geq r(b-1)$ or $r\,|\,a$.' For r∤a, U=[1,1+floor(a/r)], excess 0.
(b) AHT Theorem 1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArtificialZeng/AI-Has-Taste/main/reproducible_source_code/BigWIN2/BW2-PR20260914-q_product_unimodality/source/manuscript/main.tex): '[a]_q[c]_q[b]_{q^r} is weakly unimodal if and only if r\mid a or r\mid c or b\le1+\lfloor a/r\rfloor+\lfloor c/r\rfloor.' Excess 0.
(c) ProveIt Thm 5.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex): 'The polynomial $(\prod_i\qi{a_i})\qir b2$ is unimodal if and only if some $a_i$ is even or b\le1+\sum_i\lfloor a_i/2\rfloor.' Excess 0.
(d) ProveIt Thm 'Sharp spacing-three criterion' (thm:r3; Thm 6.1 in round-2 numbering): 'The polynomial $P_{\boldsymbol a,b,3}$ is unimodal if and only if (\exists i\colon3\mid a_i) or b\le1+Q+2\lfloor t/6\rfloor'. Excess 2floor(t/6), even.
(e) CIMSY remark: '$([3]_{q})^{4}[2]_{q^{4}}$ is unimodal despite violating the inequality'. Numerically U={1,2,3} (round 2), max 3 ≡ 1+F with F=0.
ProveIt states the open gap explicitly: 'The residue classes decide what happens in the possible gap' (after the sandwich eq.). It neither proves nor states a parity or closure rule. Not found: non-interval U, the step-2 tail {N*+2,...}, closure b->b-2, and max U ≡ 1+F in general.

per_claim.claim: R3: Conjecture S2. U = [1,B*] or U = [1,B*] minus {B*-1}.
per_claim.evidence: Only the interval alternative appears, and only in the classified ranges: r=2 (ProveIt Thm 5.1), r=3 (ProveIt Thm 6.1 and Cor. cor:binomialexact '(1+q)^t\qir B3 is unimodal \Longleftrightarrow t\ge6\lfloor B/2\rfloor'), k=1 (CIMSY Prop 5.3) and k=2 (AHT Thm 1). All quoted verbatim under R2, links https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArtificialZeng/AI-Has-Taste/main/reproducible_source_code/BigWIN2/BW2-PR20260914-q_product_unimodality/source/manuscript/main.tex , https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12822. The second alternative (one missing value B*-1) and the global S2 dichotomy for r>=4 were not found. ProveIt writes: 'For $r\ge4$, a general classification of $(\prod_i\qi{a_i})\qir b r$ is not obtained here.'

per_claim.claim: R4: Cyclic unimodality of residue-class sums. The sums of coefficients of a product of q-integers in each class mod r are unimodal around the cycle Z/r, peaked at the centre.
per_claim.evidence:
No source states this. Adjacent material:
(1) ProveIt (link above) defines exactly these sums, 'R_s=\sum_{0\le j\le S,\ j\equiv s (r)} f_j ... The $R_s$ are the total coefficient masses in the residue classes modulo $r$', and proves only 'The $R_s$ cannot all be equal' (proof of Thm 4.2). It uses symmetry, 'Symmetry of $F$ implies $R_0=R_{r-1}$'. It says nothing about cyclic unimodality.
(2) Krason-Milewski arXiv:1905.11815 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.11815), Theorem 4.3: 'Let k, l be positive integers such that gcd(k, l) = 1 and r any positive divisor of l. For any i ∈ Z/rZ we have \sum p(k, l-1, j ≡ i mod r) = (1/r) binom(k+l-1, l-1)'. Remark 4.6: 'the left hand side of (4.35) is the sum ... over the moduli classes modulo r of the coefficients of the Gaussian polynomial'. This concerns Gaussian polynomials (quotients), not products of q-integers. Their Example 4.8 (k=l=6, r=6) lists class sums '80, 75, 78, 76, 78, 75'. These are not cyclically unimodal (local maxima at classes 0, 2, 4), so the R4 phenomenon does not extend to Gaussian polynomials. Problem 4.16 there, 'Find relations between sums over moduli classes modulo d of coefficients of Gaussian polynomials', is open in that paper.
(3) Dolgopyat-Hafouta arXiv:2011.14852 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14852), abstract: 'the distance between the distribution of the underlying partial sums modulo some $h\in \bbN$ and the uniform distribution could fail to be $o(σ_N^{1-r})$'. This is the probabilistic role of residue-class masses. It gives no unimodality-on-the-cycle statement.

per_claim.claim: R5: Exact rule for the all-equal family [a]_q^k [b]_{q^r}. The excess B*-1-F grows linearly in k with a -ln k correction (entropy/Stirling asymptotics of the coefficients of 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r))).
per_claim.evidence:
Special cases of the exact rule are in the literature (quoted verbatim). The general rule and the -ln k asymptotics were not found.
(a) a=2, r=3 (ProveIt Cor. 'A two-parameter infinite family' (label cor:binomialexact), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex): 'For $t\ge0$ and $B\ge1$, (1+q)^t\qir B3 is unimodal \Longleftrightarrow t\ge6\lfloor B/2\rfloor.' Here the excess is 2floor(k/6), linear in k with no log term.
(b) a=2, b=2, any r: Handelman arXiv:1102.2961 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.2961), abstract: 'Let m and k ≥ 2 be positive integers. We show that polynomial P = (1 + x)^m (1 + x^k) is strongly unimodal (frequently known as log concave) if and only if m ≥ k^2 − 3; this is also the criterion for P to be merely unimodal'. Mapping: m=k (number of factors), k=r. This gives only the first jump of B* (from 1 to at least 2). ProveIt's 'Sharp two-shift smoothing threshold' theorem (thm:twoshift) reproves it, with table row: 'Gap r & First unimodal exponent r^2-3'.
(c) k=1 and k=2: CIMSY Prop 5.3 and AHT Thm 1 (quoted under R2).
(d) Asymptotic toolkit, framework only: the Almkvist zbMATH review (Zbl 0624.20028, https://zbmath.org/?q=an:0624.20028) says '...the author proves it for n=4, using analytic methods of A. Odlyzko and B. Richmond to estimate the coefficients.' Also restricted-partition quasi-polynomials and Sylvester waves, and Dolgopyat-Hafouta Edgeworth expansions with mod-h obstructions. None treats [a]^k[b]_{q^r}.
Our computed jump points for a=2, r=4 (k = 13, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 77, 87 for B* = 3, 5, ..., 17) are not in OEIS. The first one equals Handelman's r^2-3 = 13.

per_claim.claim: R6: Large-part stabilization. Once all a_i exceed an explicit threshold, U depends only on the residues (shifted by F).
per_claim.evidence:
Not found as stated. Related:
(1) ProveIt Cor 3.3 ('Reduction to small residues', https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex): 'Suppose no $a_i$ is divisible by $r$, and write a_i=rA_i+s_i ... If $b>Q+1$ and (\prod_i\qi{s_i})\qir{b-Q}{r} is $\SU$, then $P_{\boldsymbol a,b,r}$ is $\SU$.' ProveIt then adds: 'Corollary~\ref{cor:core} is a sufficient reduction, not an assertion that residue reduction preserves unimodality in both directions for every $r$.' So the shift by F is in the literature, but only in the sufficient direction and with no threshold.
(2) In every classified range (r=2, r=3, k<=2) the answer depends only on residues and F, so stabilization holds trivially there with threshold 0 (statements under R2).
(3) Almkvist (zbMATH Zbl 0678.05002, https://zbmath.org/?q=an:0678.05002): 'The author investigates the well-known conjecture that the polynomial \prod^{r}_{\nu =1}(1-t^{n\nu})/(1-t^{\nu}) is symmetric unimodal if n is even and r\geq 1, or n is odd and r\geq 11 ... The method of proof makes use of a clever induction for "large" r'. This is a different stabilization: more stretched factors, a different family.

per_claim.claim: R7: Closed form for exactly three 'middle' residues.
per_claim.evidence: No source treats three factors with residues in [2,r-2] for r>=4. The nearest results are AHT Thm 1 (two ordinary factors, all r) and ProveIt Thm 6.1 (r=3, which has no middle residues), quoted under R2. ProveIt says: 'the necessity question for two or three ordinary factors at those spacings is not settled by the present arguments' and '\emph{open} here for $k\le3$ with $r\ge4$' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/main/SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/log-concavity-and-unimodality/q-integer-product-unimodality/report.tex).

per_claim.claim: R8: Counterexample to a 'local' parity-gap statement at r ≈ 8595 (only the global S2 survives).
per_claim.evidence: No such counterexample or parity-gap statement was found. The known counterexamples in the literature concern the necessity clause of CIMSY Conj 5.4: ProveIt Prop. 'Exact disproof' (prop:counterexample) and Cor. 'A log-concave infinite family' (cor:infinite) ('For every $n\ge6$, the polynomial $\qi2^{\,n}\qir23=(1+q)^n(1+q^3)$ is a log-concave counterexample to the necessity assertion of [Conjecture 5.4]'), trureturing's Lean certificate of (1+q)^6(1+q^3), and the CIMSY remark on ([3]_q)^4[2]_{q^4}. None involves large r or parity gaps.

summary: Round 3 literature search, 48 logged queries across GitHub code/repo search, WebSearch, the export.arxiv.org API (working this round), zbMATH Open, MathOverflow/StackExchange and OEIS. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate-limited. No new repository or paper on CIMSY Conj 5.4 appeared since round 2: the ProveIt and AI-Has-Taste files are byte-identical to the round-2 copies, the GitHub hits are the same 34, and the 40 newest math.CO unimodality papers through 2026-09-30 contain nothing relevant. Status: R1 文献连线, R2 文献连线, R3 文献连线, R4 未找到, R5 文献连线, R6 文献连线, R7 未找到, R8 未找到. No claim is 文献已有. R1 connects to ProveIt Lemma 4.1 (tail differences = residue-mass differences), AHT's k=2 counting differences, and Xin-Zhong/Abdallah-McDaniel parity-class ideas. R2 and R3 contain only the interval case (U=[1,B*] with even excess), which is all the literature proves (r=2, r=3, k=1, k=2). R5 contains the a=2, r=3 exact rule (ProveIt Cor. 'A two-parameter infinite family' (label cor:binomialexact): t>=6floor(B/2)) and Handelman's b=2 threshold k>=r^2-3. The jump sequence 13, 25, 35, ... for a=2, r=4 is not in OEIS. R6 matches ProveIt Cor 3.3 (one-directional reduction to residues). New sources this round: Almkvist 1987/1989 zbMATH reviews (Zbl 0624.20028, Zbl 0678.05002), Abdallah-McDaniel ALCO 2025 Thm 1.3 (H(m,2)=[m]_t[m]_{t^2} unimodal iff m even; k=1 case), Krason-Milewski arXiv:1905.11815 (residue-class sums of Gaussian polynomials; their Example 4.8 shows such sums need not be cyclically unimodal for Gaussian polynomials, a useful contrast for R4), and Dolgopyat-Hafouta arXiv:2011.14852 (Edgeworth expansions with mod-h obstructions).
